name: An Apple Custard
description: Historical recipe from The Virginia Housewife; Or, Methodical Cook (1824). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: rich boiled custard
ingredients.originalText: a quart of rich boiled custard

instructions.text: Pare and core twelve pippins, slice them tolerably thick
Put a pound of loaf sugar in a stew pan, with a pint of water and twelve cloves
Boil and skim it, then put in the apples, and stew them till clear, and but little of the syrup remains
Lay them in a deep dish, and take out the cloves
When the apples are cold, pour in a quart of rich boiled custard
Set it in water, and make it boil till the custard is set
Take care the water does not get into it

source.author: Mary Randolph
source.originalInstructions:
1. Pare and core twelve pippins, slice them tolerably thick
2. Put a pound of loaf sugar in a stew pan, with a pint of water and twelve cloves
3. Boil and skim it, then put in the apples, and stew them till clear, and but little of the syrup remains
4. Lay them in a deep dish, and take out the cloves
5. When the apples are cold, pour in a quart of rich boiled custard
6. Set it in water, and make it boil till the custard is set
7. Take care the water does not get into it
